fm.title: Discontinuities
fm.description: Dead zone, relay, and saturation nonlinearities (6 blocks)

rows.intent: Output zero while the input is within a dead band, then pass the offset beyond it — use to model backlash or ignore small signals.
Switch the output between two values with hysteresis around on/off thresholds — use for bang-bang control or thermostat-like logic.
Clip a signal to specified upper and lower limits — use to enforce actuator or physical bounds.
Output zero for inputs within a dead zone. Offset input signals by either the Start or End value when outside of the dead zone.
Bound the range of the second input by using the first input (upper limit) and the third input (lower limit).
If the input is above the threshold, the output is zero, otherwise the output equals the input.

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Additional Math & Discrete/Additional Math: Increment - Decrement/Decrement Real World

rows.intent: Increase the Real World Value of Signal by 1.0 Overflows will always wrap.
Delay a signal by a configurable number of sample steps — use to align timing or model transport delay in discrete systems.
Accumulate a signal over time in discrete steps, with optional limits and reset — use for discrete integration in controllers and estimators.
Hold the input for one sample period (z^-1) — use to introduce a one-step delay or break an algebraic loop.
Output the current input value minus the previous input value.

fm.description: Logical, relational, and bit operations (18 blocks)

rows.intent: Perform the specified bitwise operation on the inputs. The output data type should represent zero exactly.
Map inputs to outputs via a truth table — use to implement combinational logic or state-machine output tables.
Apply a logical operation (AND/OR/NOT/XOR/…) to boolean inputs — use for boolean decision logic.
Compare two inputs (==, <, >, …) and output a boolean — use to build conditions and thresholds.
Shift bits or the binary point of a signal — use for fast multiply/divide by powers of two or fixed-point rescaling.
Clear ith bit of the stored integer to 0. Scaling is ignored.
Set ith bit of the stored integer to 1. Scaling is ignored.

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Compare To Constant
rows.intent: Determine how a signal compares to a constant.

rows.intent: Determine how a signal compares to zero.
If the input does not equal its previous value, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the previous input U/z.
If the input is strictly less than its previous value, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the previous input U/z.

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Detect Fall Negative
rows.intent: If the input is strictly negative and its previous value was nonnegative, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the boolean expression (U/z < 0).

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Detect Fall Nonpositive
rows.intent: If the input is nonpositive and its previous value was strictly positive, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the boolean expression (U/z <= 0).
If the input is strictly greater than its previous value, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the previous input U/z.

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Detect Rise Nonnegative
rows.intent: If the input is nonnegative and its previous value was strictly negative, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the boolean expression (U/z >= 0).

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Detect Rise Positive
rows.intent: If the input is strictly positive and its previous value was nonpositive, then output TRUE, otherwise output FALSE. The initial condition determines the initial value of the boolean expression (U/z > 0).
If the input is in the interval between the lower limit and the upper limit, then the output is TRUE, otherwise it is FALSE.

rows.ref: do178Lib/Simulink/Logic and Bit Operations/Interval Test Dynamic
rows.intent: If the input is in the interval between the lower limit and the upper limit, then the output is TRUE, otherwise it is FALSE.

fm.title: Lookup tables
fm.description: N-D lookup tables and prelookup interpolation (6 blocks)

rows.intent: Map one input to an output by interpolating breakpoint-value pairs — use for calibration curves and nonlinear functions.
Interpolate an output from two inputs over a gridded table — use for two-variable maps such as gain schedules.
Interpolate an output from three inputs over a gridded table — use for three-variable characterization maps.
Interpolate table values using the index/fraction from a Prelookup block — use for efficient multi-table lookups that share breakpoints.
Compute the index and fraction of an input within a breakpoint set — use ahead of Interpolation Using Prelookup to share breakpoint search.
Interpolate an output from N inputs over an N-dimensional table — use for multi-variable calibration maps.

fm.title: Math
fm.description: Arithmetic and elementwise math functions (21 blocks)

rows.intent: Output the absolute value (magnitude) of the input — use to remove sign or compute magnitude.
Sum inputs with configurable signs — use for additive combination of signals.
Write values into selected elements of a signal or array — use to update specific elements of a vector or matrix.
Add a constant offset to the input — use to shift a signal by a fixed amount.
Multiply and/or divide inputs — use for ratios, normalization, or scaling by another signal.
Compute the dot (inner) product of two vectors — use for projections, weighted sums, or magnitude-squared.
Scale a signal by a constant factor — use for unit conversion, controller gains, or applying physical constants.
Apply a math function (exp, log, power, mod, reciprocal, …) — use for elementwise nonlinear math.
Output the minimum or maximum across inputs or elements — use to select extremes or clamp between signals.
Evaluate a polynomial with given coefficients at the input — use to apply a polynomial fit or characteristic.
Multiply inputs elementwise or as matrices — use for scaling, modulation, or products of signals.
Change the dimensions of a signal without changing its data — use to convert between vector and matrix shapes.
Round a signal (floor, ceil, round, fix) — use to quantize to integers or control rounding behavior.
Output the sign (-1/0/+1) of the input — use for direction detection or sign extraction.
Compute a sign-preserving square root, sign(u)·sqrt(|u|) — use when the input can be negative but root-like scaling is needed.
Compute the square root of the input — use for magnitude, RMS, or geometric calculations.
Subtract inputs (a Sum configured for subtraction) — use to compute differences or control errors.
Add or subtract inputs per the sign list — use to combine signals, form errors, or accumulate.
Apply a trig function (sin, cos, tan, atan2, …) — use for angle/phase computation and coordinate transforms.
Negate the input (multiply by -1) — use to invert a signal's sign.
Output the max or min of all past inputs u. The output is reset to the initial condition when the Reset input signal R is TRUE. This reset action is vectorized and supports scalar expansion.

fm.title: Ports subsystems
fm.description: Ports, subsystems, and control-flow containers (19 blocks)

rows.intent: Inport that brings a signal into a subsystem or model — use to define an input interface.

Execute function-call subsystems, models, or Stateflow charts that are connected to this block at a specified rate. To execute multiple function-call blocks in prescribed order, use this block in conjunction with a Function-Call Split block. The 'Sample time' parameter specifies the rate at which this block executes each function-call block connected to it. To iteratively execute each function-call block connected to this block multiple times at each time step, use the 'Number of iterations' parameter. If you check 'Show enable port' checkbox, block outputs function-call signal only when input signal to the enable port has positive scalar value.
Split one function-call line to trigger multiple subsystems — use to invoke several function-call subsystems from one caller.
Evaluate if/elseif conditions and issue action outputs — use with If Action Subsystems for conditional execution.
Route control to case actions based on an integer input — use with Case Action Subsystems for multiway branching.
Outport that sends a signal out of a subsystem or model — use to define an output interface.
Group blocks that execute atomically as a single unit — use to enforce single-unit execution and code-generation boundaries.
Execute contained blocks only while an enable signal is positive — use for conditionally-run logic.
Run the contained logic independently on each element/slice of an input — use to vectorize per-element processing.
Execute the contents a fixed number of iterations per step — use for bounded loops.
Execute the contents when invoked by a function-call — use for event- or scheduler-driven logic.
Contained action executed when driven by an If block branch — use as the body of a conditional branch.
Group blocks into a hierarchical container — use to organize a model into reusable, readable units.
Execute the contents on a trigger edge — use for edge-driven, event-based logic.
Contain multiple implementations and activate one by variant condition — use to switch between design alternatives.
Execute the contents repeatedly while a condition holds — use for condition-controlled loops.

Set the Data Type and Scaling of the propagated signal based on information from the reference signals. Notes: 1) Items closer to the top of the dialog have higher priority/precedence. a) Reference inputs of type double have priority over all others. b) Singles have priority over integer and fixed point data types. c) Multiplicative adjustments are carried out before additive adjustments. d) Number-of-Bits is determined before the precision or positive-range is inherited from the reference signals. 2) PosRange is one bit higher than the exact maximum positive range of the signal. 3) The computed Number-of-Bits is promoted to the smallest allowable value that is greater than or equal to the computation. If none exists, then the block returns an error.
Outport that sends a signal out of a subsystem or model — use to define an output interface.
Inport that brings a signal into a subsystem or model — use to define an input interface.

rows.intent: Force multiple signals to share the same data type — use to keep interfaces type-consistent.
Convert a signal to a specified data type — use to set integer/fixed-point type and scaling.
Set the initial value of a signal for the first time step — use to seed states or feedback at start-up.
Output signal attributes such as width, sample time, complexity, and dimensions — use to inspect properties at runtime.
Safely transfer data between blocks running at different sample rates — use to handle multirate signal hand-off.
Convert a signal's storage form (contiguous copy, bus, virtual) — use to satisfy downstream signal requirements.
Assert and enforce a signal's attributes (type, dimensions, sample time) — use to document and check interfaces.
Convert a signal between physical units — use to reconcile unit mismatches between components.
Output the number of elements in the input signal — use to obtain vector width at runtime.

Convert the second input to the data type and scaling of the first input. The conversion has two possible goals. One goal is to have the Real World Values of the input and the output be equal. The other goal is to have the Stored Integer Values of the input and the output be equal. Overflows and quantization errors can prevent the goal from being fully achieved.

Read the current value of a data store — use to consume shared data.

Split a vector signal into separate scalar/subvector lines — use to break out combined signals.
Receive a signal from a matching Goto tag — use for wireless routing to reduce diagram clutter.
Send a signal to matching From blocks via a tag — use for wireless routing to reduce diagram clutter.

Route one of several data inputs to the output based on a control index — use for index-selected multiplexing.
Combine several signals into a single vector line — use to bundle scalars for compact routing.
Select a subset of elements from a signal by index — use to extract specific channels or samples.
Pass one of two inputs based on a control threshold — use for conditional signal selection.
Concatenate inputs into a larger vector or matrix — use to assemble composite signals.

Cap an unused output port — use to avoid unconnected-line warnings.

Convert a vector of ASCII codes to a string signal — use to build text from character codes.
